gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a regional bank currently experiencing acute liquidity stress and margin compression that obscures its long-term earnings power

gate2.why_available: The market is reacting to a contagion-driven confidence shock that has triggered a deposit run, overshadowing the bank's historical performance and customer loyalty [D01, D05]. Buffett would look past the temporary panic to evaluate whether the underlying franchise, particularly its affluent client relationships, remains intact once the liquidity pressure is stabilized [D01]. The value will show up as deposit stability returns and market sentiment normalizes, allowing the bank's core earnings power to re-emerge [D01, D07].
evidence: Acute stress from a deposit run by affluent clients with large uninsured balances [D05].
Bank is positioned as a sound lending franchise currently facing a regional-bank confidence shock [D01].
Eleven large banks provided $30 billion in deposits on March 16, 2023, to bolster liquidity [D07].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market assumes that a regional bank confidence shock and asset-liability duration mismatches will lead to a permanent impairment of the institution's deposit franchise and earnings power [D05].
what_must_be_true: The bank's affluent client base remains loyal and does not fully migrate to systemic institutions.
The $30 billion deposit injection is sufficient to bridge the liquidity gap without permanent equity dilution.
The bank's long-term earnings potential is not structurally impaired by higher wholesale funding costs.

final.memo:
We have reviewed the business of the bank, which operates as a relationship lender and wealth manager for affluent clients [D01]. While the company has historically shown consistent growth, with net income rising 12.7% in 2022, the current environment presents challenges that we do not care to navigate [D01].

The bank is presently suffering from acute liquidity stress and a deposit run that threatens its fundamental stability [D05]. We have no way of knowing whether its affluent client base will remain loyal or if the $30 billion in recent liquidity support from peers will be sufficient to prevent permanent impairment of equity [D05, D07].

Banking is inherently capital-intensive, and the current asset-liability mismatch is a dangerous combination when confidence vanishes [D05]. We prefer to put our money to work in businesses where the economics are near-certain, rather than in situations where we must guess if the institution will survive a run on its deposits [D05, D08].

At present, we hold $128.6 billion in cash and T-bills [D08]. We are perfectly content to sit on our hands when we cannot see why we should get a bargain or where we can be sure of protecting Berkshire's capital and reputation. We are passing on this opportunity.
